  </g>
  <text x="930" y="220" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#4A90D9">THE SOLUTION</text>
  <text x="930" y="255" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#64748B">Efficient architectures</text>
  <text x="930" y="280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#64748B">MoE + Attention Innovation</text>
  <text x="930" y="340" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="48" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">✓</text>
  <text x="930" y="400" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">DeepSeek-V2: 236B total / 21B active</text>

  <!-- Bottom insight box -->
  <rect x="60" y="500" width="1160" height="120" rx="8" fill="#1A1A2E"/>
  <text x="90" y="545" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#D97757">KEY INSIGHT</text>
  <text x="90" y="580" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#FFFFFF">Standard MHA (Multi-Head Attention) stores full K/V per head per token — creating a memory bottleneck</text>
  <text x="90" y="605" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#FFFFFF">that grows linearly with context length. This KV cache problem makes long-context inference prohibitively expensive.</text>

  <!-- Footer -->
  <text x="640" y="690" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B" text-anchor="middle">2</text>
</svg>

  <!-- Title -->
  <text x="60" y="100" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="32" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">
    DeepSeek-V2 Architecture: MLA + DeepSeekMoE in a Transformer Block
  </text>

  <!-- Main architecture diagram area -->
  <g transform="translate(60, 160)">
    <!-- Input token -->
    <rect x="0" y="120" width="140" height="60" rx="6" fill="#1A1A2E"/>
    <text x="70" y="155" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF" text-anchor="middle">Input Token</text>

    <!-- Arrow -->
    <text x="160" y="155" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="24" fill="#64748B" text-anchor="middle">→</text>

    <!-- MLA Layer -->
    <g filter="url(#cardShadow)">
      <rect x="190" y="40" width="320" height="200" rx="8" fill="#F8FAFC" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1"/>
      <rect x="190" y="40" width="320" height="8" fill="#4A90D9"/>
    </g>
    <text x="350" y="80" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#4A90D9" text-anchor="middle">MLA</text>
    <text x="350" y="105" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#64748B" text-anchor="middle">Multi-Head Latent Attention</text>
    <text x="220" y="140" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">• Low-rank KV compression</text>
    <text x="220" y="165" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">• Decoupled RoPE</text>
    <text x="220" y="190" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">• 93.3% cache reduction</text>
    <text x="220" y="215" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">• Better than MHA performance</text>

    <!-- Arrow -->
    <text x="530" y="155" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="24" fill="#64748B" text-anchor="middle">→</text>

    <!-- DeepSeekMoE Layer -->
    <g filter="url(#cardShadow)">
      <rect x="560" y="40" width="320" height="200" rx="8" fill="#F8FAFC" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1"/>
      <rect x="560" y="40" width="320" height="8" fill="#10B981"/>
    </g>
    <text x="720" y="80" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#10B981" text-anchor="middle">DeepSeekMoE</text>
    <text x="720" y="105" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#64748B" text-anchor="middle">Mixture-of-Experts FFN</text>
    <text x="590" y="140" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">• Shared experts (always active)</text>
    <text x="590" y="165" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">• Routed experts (top-K selection)</text>
    <text x="590" y="190" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">• Fine-grained specialization</text>
    <text x="590" y="215" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">• Device-limited routing</text>

    <!-- Arrow -->
    <text x="900" y="155" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="24" fill="#64748B" text-anchor="middle">→</text>

    <!-- Output -->
    <rect x="930" y="120" width="140" height="60" rx="6" fill="#D97757"/>
    <text x="1000" y="155" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF" text-anchor="middle">Output</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Bottom description cards -->
  <g transform="translate(60, 420)">
    <!-- MLA Card -->
    <g filter="url(#cardShadow)">
      <rect x="0" y="0" width="550" height="180" rx="8" fill="#F8FAFC" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1"/>
      <rect x="0" y="0" width="550" height="6" fill="#4A90D9"/>
    </g>
    <text x="30" y="45" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#4A90D9">Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA)</text>
    <text x="30" y="80" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">Instead of caching full K/V vectors per head, MLA compresses them into a compact</text>
    <text x="30" y="102" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">latent vector c_t^KV. Full keys/values are reconstructed on-the-fly via learned</text>
    <text x="30" y="124" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">projection matrices — achieving better performance than standard MHA while</text>
    <text x="30" y="146" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">dramatically reducing the KV cache size.</text>

    <!-- DeepSeekMoE Card -->
    <g filter="url(#cardShadow)">
      <rect x="600" y="0" width="550" height="180" rx="8" fill="#F8FAFC" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1"/>
      <rect x="600" y="0" width="550" height="6" fill="#10B981"/>
    </g>
    <text x="630" y="45" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#10B981">DeepSeekMoE FFN</text>
    <text x="630" y="80" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">Fine-grained expert segmentation increases specialization potential.</text>
    <text x="630" y="102" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">Shared experts capture common knowledge; routed experts are sparsely</text>
    <text x="630" y="124" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">activated via top-K routing. Device-limited routing reduces cross-node</text>
    <text x="630" y="146" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">communication overhead.</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Footer -->
  <text x="640" y="690" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B" text-anchor="middle">3</text>
</svg>

    <linearGradient id="orangeBar" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#D97757"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#E8956F"/>
    </linearGradient>
    <linearGradient id="blueGrad" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="0%" y2="100%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#4A90D9"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#3A7BC8"/>
    </linearGradient>
    <linearGradient id="greenGrad" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="0%" y2="100%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#10B981"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#0D9668"/>
    </linearGradient>
    <filter id="cardShadow" x="-5%" y="-5%" width="110%" height="115%">
      <feDropShadow dx="0" dy="2" stdDeviation="4" flood-color="#1A1A2E" flood-opacity="0.1"/>
    </filter>
  </defs>

  <!-- Background -->
  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF"/>

  <!-- Top orange bar -->
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="6" fill="url(#orangeBar)"/>

  <!-- Page label -->
  <text x="60" y="55" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#D97757" letter-spacing="2">ARCHITECTURE</text>

  <!-- Title -->
  <text x="60" y="100" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="32" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">
    DeepSeek-V2 Architecture: MLA + DeepSeekMoE in a Transformer Block
  </text>

  <!-- Main architecture diagram area -->
  <g transform="translate(60, 160)">
    <!-- Input token -->
    <rect x="0" y="120" width="140" height="60" rx="6" fill="#1A1A2E"/>
    <text x="70" y="155" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF" text-anchor="middle">Input Token</text>

    <!-- Arrow -->
    <text x="160" y="155" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="24" fill="#64748B" text-anchor="middle">→</text>

    <!-- MLA Layer -->
    <g filter="url(#cardShadow)">
      <rect x="190" y="40" width="320" height="200" rx="8" fill="#F8FAFC" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1"/>
      <rect x="190" y="40" width="320" height="8" fill="#4A90D9"/>
    </g>
    <text x="350" y="80" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#4A90D9" text-anchor="middle">MLA</text>
    <text x="350" y="105" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#64748B" text-anchor="middle">Multi-Head Latent Attention</text>
    <text x="220" y="140" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">• Low-rank KV compression</text>
    <text x="220" y="165" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">• Decoupled RoPE</text>
    <text x="220" y="190" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">• 93.3% cache reduction</text>
    <text x="220" y="215" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">• Better than MHA performance</text>

    <!-- Arrow -->
    <text x="530" y="155" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="24" fill="#64748B" text-anchor="middle">→</text>

    <!-- DeepSeekMoE Layer -->
    <g filter="url(#cardShadow)">
      <rect x="560" y="40" width="320" height="200" rx="8" fill="#F8FAFC" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1"/>
      <rect x="560" y="40" width="320" height="8" fill="#10B981"/>
    </g>
    <text x="720" y="80" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#10B981" text-anchor="middle">DeepSeekMoE</text>
    <text x="720" y="105" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#64748B" text-anchor="middle">Mixture-of-Experts FFN</text>
    <text x="590" y="140" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">• Shared experts (always active)</text>
    <text x="590" y="165" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">• Routed experts (top-K selection)</text>
    <text x="590" y="190" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">• Fine-grained specialization</text>
    <text x="590" y="215" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">• Device-limited routing</text>

    <!-- Arrow -->
    <text x="900" y="155" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="24" fill="#64748B" text-anchor="middle">→</text>

    <!-- Output -->
    <rect x="930" y="120" width="140" height="60" rx="6" fill="#D97757"/>
    <text x="1000" y="155" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF" text-anchor="middle">Output</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Bottom description cards -->
  <g transform="translate(60, 420)">
    <!-- MLA Card -->
    <g filter="url(#cardShadow)">
      <rect x="0" y="0" width="550" height="180" rx="8" fill="#F8FAFC" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1"/>
      <rect x="0" y="0" width="550" height="6" fill="#4A90D9"/>
    </g>
    <text x="30" y="45" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#4A90D9">Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA)</text>
    <text x="30" y="80" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">Instead of caching full K/V vectors per head, MLA compresses them into a compact</text>
    <text x="30" y="102" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">latent vector c_t^KV. Full keys/values are reconstructed on-the-fly via learned</text>
    <text x="30" y="124" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">projection matrices — achieving better performance than standard MHA while</text>
    <text x="30" y="146" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">dramatically reducing the KV cache size.</text>

    <!-- DeepSeekMoE Card -->
    <g filter="url(#cardShadow)">
      <rect x="600" y="0" width="550" height="180" rx="8" fill="#F8FAFC" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1"/>
      <rect x="600" y="0" width="550" height="6" fill="#10B981"/>
    </g>
    <text x="630" y="45" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#10B981">DeepSeekMoE FFN</text>
    <text x="630" y="80" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">Fine-grained expert segmentation increases specialization potential.</text>
    <text x="630" y="102" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">Shared experts capture common knowledge; routed experts are sparsely</text>
    <text x="630" y="124" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">activated via top-K routing. Device-limited routing reduces cross-node</text>
    <text x="630" y="146" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">communication overhead.</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Footer -->
  <text x="640" y="690" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B" text-anchor="middle">3</text>
</svg>

# 01_cover

DeepSeek-V2 represents a breakthrough in Mixture-of-Experts language model design, achieving top-tier open-source LLM performance while activating only 21 billion of its 236 billion total parameters. This technical presentation explores the two core architectural innovations — Multi-Head Latent Attention and DeepSeekMoE — that make this efficiency possible.

Key points: (1) 236B total / 21B activated parameters (2) 128K context length support (3) Paper reference: arxiv.org/abs/2405.04434

Duration: 1 minute

Key points: (1) SFT + GRPO RL pipeline (2) Strong English and Chinese benchmarks (3) Outperforms closed-source models on Chinese

[Transition] Let us summarize the key findings from this technical deep-dive.

First, MLA achieves superior performance to MHA while reducing KV cache by 93.3%, making it a strictly better alternative for inference efficiency. Second, DeepSeekMoE with fine-grained experts and shared expert isolation enables training a 236B-parameter model at 42.5% lower cost than a 67B dense model. The architectural innovations in DeepSeek-V2 demonstrate that efficient scaling is possible — we do not have to choose between performance and cost.

Key points: (1) MLA + DeepSeekMoE = efficient architecture (2) Top-tier performance at fraction of activated params (3) Open-source availability for research and deployment

Duration: 1 minute

raw_arguments.content:
# 01_cover

DeepSeek-V2 represents a breakthrough in Mixture-of-Experts language model design, achieving top-tier open-source LLM performance while activating only 21 billion of its 236 billion total parameters. This technical presentation explores the two core architectural innovations — Multi-Head Latent Attention and DeepSeekMoE — that make this efficiency possible.

Key points: (1) 236B total / 21B activated parameters (2) 128K context length support (3) Paper reference: arxiv.org/abs/2405.04434

Duration: 1 minute

---

# 02_motivation

[Transition] To understand why DeepSeek-V2 matters, we first need to appreciate the fundamental tension in scaling large language models.

The core dilemma: larger models deliver better intelligence, but the computational costs become prohibitive. Standard Multi-Head Attention stores full key-value pairs per head per token, creating a memory bottleneck that grows linearly with context length. This KV cache problem makes long-context inference increasingly expensive as models scale.

[Pause] The industry has tried alternatives like Grouped-Query Attention and Multi-Query Attention, but these sacrifice performance for efficiency. Neither GQA nor MQA solves the fundamental problem — they merely make tradeoffs.

Key points: (1) KV cache is the memory bottleneck in LLM inference (2) GQA and MQA trade performance for reduced memory (3) We need a solution that improves both efficiency AND performance

Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 03_architecture

[Transition] DeepSeek-V2 addresses this challenge with a novel architecture that combines two innovations within each Transformer block.

The Multi-Head Latent Attention mechanism replaces standard attention. Instead of storing full K and V vectors, MLA compresses them into a compact latent vector that is cached during inference. Full keys and values are reconstructed on-the-fly via learned projection matrices.

The DeepSeekMoE FFN layers replace dense feedforward networks with a mixture-of-experts approach. Fine-grained expert segmentation increases specialization potential, while shared experts capture common knowledge across all tokens.

Together, these innovations enable the dramatic efficiency gains we will see later.

Key points: (1) MLA provides low-rank KV compression (2) DeepSeekMoE enables sparse activation (3) Both innovations work together in each Transformer block

Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 04_mla

[Transition] Let us dive deeper into Multi-Head Latent Attention, the first core innovation.

The key insight behind MLA is low-rank key-value joint compression. Standard MHA stores full K/V per head per token — with 8K context, this creates enormous memory pressure. MLA compresses this into a compact latent vector, reducing cache requirements by 93.3%.

How does it work? First, the model compresses K and V into a low-dimensional latent vector during the forward pass. Second, at inference time, it reconstructs full K and V on-the-fly via learned projection matrices. Third, decoupled RoPE handles positional information separately, avoiding interference with the compression.

The result: better performance than standard MHA while using dramatically less cache. This is not a tradeoff — it is a genuine improvement.

Key points: (1) 93.3% KV cache reduction (2) Better than MHA performance (3) Decoupled RoPE maintains positional awareness

Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 05_deepseek_moe

[Transition] The second core innovation is DeepSeekMoE, which replaces dense feedforward layers with a mixture-of-experts architecture.

DeepSeekMoE uses two types of experts. Shared experts are always activated and capture common knowledge that should be accessible to all tokens. Routed experts are selectively activated via top-K routing — each token only activates a small subset of experts, enabling sparse computation.

Fine-grained expert segmentation increases specialization potential — more, smaller experts can develop more targeted capabilities. Device-limited routing constrains each token to experts on at most M devices, reducing expensive cross-node communication. Auxiliary losses prevent expert collapse or underutilization.

Together with MLA, DeepSeekMoE enables training a 236B parameter model that activates only 21B parameters per token.

Key points: (1) Shared + routed experts for common vs specialized knowledge (2) Top-K sparse activation reduces compute (3) Device-limited routing enables efficient distributed training

Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 06_efficiency

[Transition] Now for the concrete results — the efficiency gains speak for themselves.

Compared to DeepSeek 67B, the previous generation dense model, DeepSeek-V2 achieves: 42.5% reduction in training costs — making it far more economical to train; 93.3% reduction in KV cache size — enabling longer contexts with less memory; and 5.76 times higher maximum generation throughput — meaning faster inference in production.

These are not theoretical projections. They are measured improvements that make DeepSeek-V2 practical for large-scale deployment. The 93.3% KV cache reduction directly translates to lower memory footprint and longer context windows. The 5.76x throughput improvement means more requests per second and lower latency per token.

Key points: (1) 42.5% training cost reduction (2) 93.3% KV cache reduction (3) 5.76x higher generation throughput

Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 07_mmlu

[Transition] But efficiency means nothing without competitive performance. Let us look at the MMLU benchmark results.

This scatter plot shows MMLU score versus activated parameters for major open-source models. The x-axis shows how many parameters are actually activated per token — the effective computational cost. The y-axis shows the MMLU score — the model's benchmark performance.

DeepSeek-V2, highlighted in green, sits in the Pareto-optimal zone — the best performance for its computational cost. It achieves 78.5% on MMLU while activating only 21 billion parameters. Compare this to LLaMA 3 70B, which activates 70 billion parameters but only achieves 77.0%. DeepSeek-V2 actually scores higher while using less than one-third the computational cost.

Mixtral 8x22B activates 39B parameters for 77.6% MMLU. Qwen1.5 72B activates 72B for 75.6%. DeepSeek-V2 dominates both on the efficiency-performance tradeoff.

Key points: (1) DeepSeek-V2 tops MMLU among open-source models (2) Activates 21B vs LLaMA 3 70B's 70B (3) Pareto-optimal position in efficiency-performance space

Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 08_alignment

[Transition] Strong benchmark performance is only part of the story. DeepSeek-V2 also achieves excellent alignment for conversational use.

The post-training pipeline combines Supervised Fine-Tuning on 1.5 million conversational sessions with Reinforcement Learning via GRPO — Group Relative Policy Optimization. GRPO uses group-relative baselines for stable training, producing well-aligned responses without the complexity of some alternative approaches.

On evaluation benchmarks, DeepSeek-V2 Chat (RL) achieves: 38.9% win rate on AlpacaEval 2.0's length-controlled evaluation; 8.97 out of 10 on MT-Bench; and 7.91 out of 10 on AlignBench's Chinese evaluation.

The Chinese benchmark result is particularly notable — DeepSeek-V2 outperforms all open-source models and most closed-source models on AlignBench, making it the strongest open-source chat model for Chinese conversations.

Key points: (1) SFT + GRPO RL pipeline (2) Strong English and Chinese benchmarks (3) Outperforms closed-source models on Chinese

Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 09_takeaways

[Transition] Let us summarize the key findings from this technical deep-dive.

First, MLA achieves superior performance to MHA while reducing KV cache by 93.3%, making it a strictly better alternative for inference efficiency. Second, DeepSeekMoE with fine-grained experts and shared expert isolation enables training a 236B-parameter model at 42.5% lower cost than a 67B dense model. Third, only 21B activated parameters are needed to match or exceed 70B-class dense models on MMLU. Fourth, the 5.76x throughput improvement over DeepSeek 67B makes DeepSeek-V2 practical for large-scale deployment. Fifth, DeepSeek-V2 Chat (RL) is the strongest open-source chat model in Chinese and competitive with closed-source systems in English evaluation.

The architectural innovations in DeepSeek-V2 demonstrate that efficient scaling is possible — we do not have to choose between performance and cost.

Key points: (1) MLA + DeepSeekMoE = efficient architecture (2) Top-tier performance at fraction of activated params (3) Open-source availability for research and deployment

Duration: 1 minute

**Presentation complete.** The 9-slide PPT has been saved to `/app/output/final_deck.pptx`.

**Slide summary:**
1. **Cover** - DeepSeek-V2 title with key stats (236B/21B, 128K context)
2. **Motivation** - LLM scaling dilemma: performance vs. cost/KV cache
3. **Architecture Overview** - MLA + DeepSeekMoE in Transformer block
4. **MLA Mechanism** - 93.3% KV cache reduction via low-rank compression
5. **DeepSeekMoE** - Fine-grained experts with shared/routed expert isolation
6. **Efficiency Gains** - 42.5% cost ↓, 93.3% cache ↓, 5.76× throughput ↑
7. **MMLU Comparison** - Scatter plot showing DeepSeek-V2's Pareto-optimal position
8. **Alignment Results** - SFT + GRPO RL, benchmark scores (AlpacaEval, MT-Bench, AlignBench)
9. **Takeaways** - 5 key findings summarizing architectural innovation
